Messages.Author: Tom Kassel
Messages.Body:
Waste Management looks rather useful for Brujah/!Brujah rush decks.
The utility might be increased with a frequent shuffle effect on your
library. Can you use something like Al's Army Apparatus to search for
a non-existent weapon and then shuffle your library?

Tom

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

In article <8u8roa$8m1$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,

Tom Kassel <tka...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> Waste Management looks rather useful for Brujah/!Brujah rush decks.
> The utility might be increased with a frequent shuffle effect on your
> library. Can you use something like Al's Army Apparatus to search for
> a non-existent weapon and then shuffle your library?

I guess there is nothing per se to stop you doing so, but it is
unsportsmanlike - although not actually cheating it is abusing actions.
There are tourney rules about unsportsmanlike conduct, with some harsh
penalties. But in friendly play, you are left at the mercy of the other
players - sometimes even worse!

So if you are going to do it, do it *sparingly* (i.e. not every turn to
recycle your one Minion Tap!).
;)

Alternatvely, why bother with non - existent! Use lots of Bombs /
Grenades / WP Grenades, Pier 13 Baltimore / Vast Wealths. That way you
use the explosive weapon and burn it, cycle it back into your library
via Waste management, and you can search as an action with Vast Wealth
or Arms Dealer / Als Army Apparatus (shuffling afterwards). Even better
if used on Black Cat!

Alternatively, use Saturday Night Specials and Dragons Breath Rounds.
Even better if you use Fames too!

DH

On Tue, 07 Nov 2000 13:25:56 GMT, hamd...@my-deja.com wrote:

>Maybe Final Nights needs a card called something like "World in Chaos",
>a Master Location you can tap to shuffle your deck.

As far as I know, it's always been legal to pick up your library and
shuffle it at any time; you then offer it to your predator to cut.

What has changed that I'm not aware of? I mean, it's not like
shuffling your library is guaranteed to HELP you in some fashion -
sure, perhaps if you have a Waste Management bit out, you can shuffle
your Minion Tap back in and then hope like hell it comes up closer to
the top, but this is HARDLY abusive. I'd certainly love to see
someone produce a deck that successfully did so, because we could sack
a few laws of probability in the process.

I really just don't understand, even if it is illegal to shuffle your
library at random, why it would matter somehow.

Re-shuffling a deck whose order is unknown is clearly a pointless
exercize, though many CCGs need a thorough shuffle between games
because cards become bunched by type in play. If you didn't spend
enough time on this task, as evidenced by drawing cards in clusters,
you might want to shuffle to better randomize the deck.

Once there have been additions to the bottom of the deck, the shuffle
can be valuable to bring the selected cards into play faster. In the
case of the rush deck I have been considering, the main effect of
adding a card a turn while playing perhaps 10 cards is another turn
before depleting the deck entirely. With my limited card collection it
would also allow more frequent use of a few key cards that I own in
insufficient quantities. A more generalized toolbox deck would be
better able to adapt to the opponents by recycling the most appropriate
cards. Neither of these seem terribly abusive functions, but it does
seem reasonable that there is some cost to be paid for the shuffle.

What? During games? I've never heard of such a thing. Do
people actually do this? I always thought you only shuffled
and offered the cut (a) at the beginning of a game, and (b)
when a card tells you to (eg Vast Wealth, Horrid Reality,
etc).

I mean, the rulebook may not specifically tell you not to
shuffle during games, but I think it only tells you that
you *should* shuffle before the game... and not mentioning
that you can't do it doesn't mean that you can.

> What has changed that I'm not aware of? I mean, it's not like
> shuffling your library is guaranteed to HELP you in some fashion -
> sure, perhaps if you have a Waste Management bit out, you can shuffle
> your Minion Tap back in and then hope like hell it comes up closer to
> the top, but this is HARDLY abusive. I'd certainly love to see
> someone produce a deck that successfully did so, because we could sack
> a few laws of probability in the process.

It's obvious that, if you put a Minion Tap on the bottom of
your library, and then shuffle, it *must* be at least as
close to the top as it was before, and will almost certainly
be closer.

> I really just don't understand, even if it is illegal to shuffle your
> library at random, why it would matter somehow.

Because if you know what the deck looks like beforehand
(eg you know what cards are on the bottom), you may have
a reason to want to shuffle.

Josh

>because cards become bunched by type in play. If you didn't spend
>enough time on this task, as evidenced by drawing cards in clusters,
>you might want to shuffle to better randomize the deck.

Correct. Of course, there's also the theory that you could just have
hit an isolated cluster, and that shuffling does no better than to
just produce MORE clusters - but that's part of why it's a pointless
exercise.

>Once there have been additions to the bottom of the deck, the shuffle
>can be valuable to bring the selected cards into play faster. In the

So instead of being card #70 in a library with 70 cards remaining, I
now have any of 69 different places the card could end up.
Mathematically, this is an improvement. Realistically, unless one
gets incredibly lucky and shuffles it into their top 10-20 cards, it
provides no significant benefit. A 30% chance of getting a card back
again in my next few turns is not something I'd care to gamble on -
I'd rather just add more into my deck.

In addition, your predator gets to cut your deck, adding an additional
random element and removing any chance of deliberately shuffling the
card near to the top.

>case of the rush deck I have been considering, the main effect of
>adding a card a turn while playing perhaps 10 cards is another turn
>before depleting the deck entirely. With my limited card collection it

Certainly. And for Rush decks, this would work very well, since over
the course of several turns you could "stack" the bottom of your deck
to be in perfect order (ie Bum's Rush, Torn Signpost, Flash, Immortal
Grapple, Blur, Taste) for One Last Hurrah. But you have to reach the
bottom of your deck for this to work, and if you're ousted by then, it
won't matter much - so I can't see this as being abusive at all.

It is worth noting that they put it in a Rush-clan deck. :)

>would also allow more frequent use of a few key cards that I own in
>insufficient quantities. A more generalized toolbox deck would be
>better able to adapt to the opponents by recycling the most appropriate
>cards. Neither of these seem terribly abusive functions, but it does
>seem reasonable that there is some cost to be paid for the shuffle.

I cannot see any way to guarantee that you will draw the card shuffled
thusly in any reasonable amount of time. Someone who wishes to depend
totally on luck is perfectly welcome to, IMO.
